thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Datadog (Software Engineering (SWE), entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. High, centralized bar: practical coding depth plus system design and a behavioral round that also probes past technical work. This is a qualitative synthesis, not a measured pass rate — Datadog publishes no applicant-to-offer rate in the fetched sources.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- A platform engineering leadership posting cites hands-on Java or Go experience and a distr — reported pattern, not a measured share: A platform engineering leadership posting cites hands-on Java or Go experience and a distributed-systems background as preferred. (source: https://careers.datadoghq.com/detail/7959705/, as of 2026-10-12)
- The same posting treats on-call work, incident response, postmortems and remediation as pa — reported pattern, not a measured share: The same posting treats on-call work, incident response, postmortems and remediation as part of the engineering culture for that team. (source: https://careers.datadoghq.com/detail/7959705/, as of 2026-10-12)
- Engineer-reported interview preparation notes describe practical, layered algorithmic ques — reported pattern, not a measured share: Engineer-reported interview preparation notes describe practical, layered algorithmic questions and system-design work tied to Datadog-like problems rather than verbatim puzzle questions. (source: https://interviewing.io/datadog-interview-questions, as of 2026-10-12)
Known biases of this data: Survivorship bias: public interview guides reflect people who reached or completed loops, not rejected applicants.; Self-report bias: interviewing.io content is based on conversations with engineers and cross-checked anecdotes, not Datadog HR data.; Official careers pages are employer marketing and describe the intended process, which may differ by team, level and region.; No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass; sponsorship and school patterns are therefore unstated, not negative findings.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).
